prompt.utterance: What happens if we double the batch size?

graderOnly: The batch size is batchSize in config/default.json (500, overridable with INGEST_BATCH_SIZE); doubling it means 1000.

src/batcher.js holds records in an in-memory buffer until batchSize is reached or flushIntervalMs (2000 ms) passes, and sends at most maxInFlight (4) batches at once; add() waits for the size-triggered flush, so reading pauses while all slots are busy.

Source-supported consequences of doubling: records held in memory at peak grow roughly in proportion to batch size (about maxInFlight+1 to maxInFlight+2 batches' worth); each request body (JSON { events: batch } in src/sink.js) is about twice as large; the same input needs about half as many requests; concurrency stays capped at 4 batches, so twice as many records are in flight; a retry resends the whole larger batch and a batch that exhausts retries puts twice as many records in the failed list; with slow input, more batches end by the 2000 ms timer instead of by size; the fixed 10 s request timeout in src/sink.js applies to a larger payload.
Throughput, latency under load, memory in absolute terms, and how the downstream bulk endpoint handles larger payloads cannot be determined from the repository; it depends on the downstream service.
No benchmarks, load tests, metrics, or recorded measurements exist anywhere in the repository, and the README states no performance numbers.
readline's async iterator in src/reader.js may buffer some lines ahead of the batcher; its exact effect on memory is not established by the repository.

notes: Standalone brownfield fixture. layers/00-project (pre-install commit) is a small Node ES-module ingest worker: src/batcher.js buffers records in memory and sends batches with at most maxInFlight concurrent sends, timed flush, and whole-batch retries; src/sink.js POSTs JSON to a bulk endpoint with a 10 s timeout; src/config.js loads config/default.json (batchSize 500, maxInFlight 4, flushIntervalMs 2000) with env overrides; node:test tests cover batching, concurrency cap, retries, timed flush, and config. layers/10-readme (pre-install commit) adds a README describing configuration and sending behavior with no performance figures. The installer then writes the default brownfield state (AUDITING, CycleMode UNSET); no workflow layer is needed since Navigator works outside the state machine.
